_doc: Which tool arguments name a tenant target, for hooks/tenancy_guard.py. When a session is bound to an opp (bin/ace-bind), every matching MCP write is checked against that opp's tenancy (ace-web GET /api/w/{ws}/opps/{slug}/tenancy) and refused if it points anywhere else. 'tool_pattern' is a regex on the tool NAME (suffix-matched, because hosts register plugins as mcp__plugin_ace_ace-connect__X or mcp__ace-connect__X, and connect-labs / Nova may be registered user-scope as mcp__connect_labs__X / mcp__nova__X — hooks/hooks.json's PreToolUse matcher must cover every one of those spellings or the rule never runs). Each 'args' entry maps an argument path (dot = nested key, [] = every list element) to the tenancy field(s) it must equal; a list of fields means any of them. An ABSENT argument is not checked (the tool's own default applies — see 'server_env' for tools whose tenant is fixed at server start). Read-only tools are deliberately absent: reading a shared source (e.g. copying FROM the shared HQ space into a partner space) is allowed, so upstream/source arguments are not listed. Three rule keys beyond 'args': 'operator_values' admits ACE-owned values whatever the tenancy says ('{agent_email_domain}', or '{plugin_env:KEY}' for a value from the installed .env); 'pending_fields' names tenancy fields ace-web has not shipped yet — an arg checked only against pending fields is INERT while the tenancy record lacks the key, and applies the moment the key appears; 'refuse_when_bound' refuses the tool outright in a bound session (warn mode logs it). Spec: ace-web docs/specs/2026-09-28-clone-and-release-design.md § D.

rules.name: connect-org-writes
rules._args_doc: `organization_slug` is the CALLER's org; `organization` is the org being acted ON (connect_send_llo_invite's invitee) and is present on that atom only — absent args are not checked, so this mapping is inert for the rest of the pattern. Both are needed for the same reason connect_create_opportunity maps target_organization_slug as well as organization_slug: checking only the caller leaves the subject unchecked. NOTE this is a SCOPE check (which orgs may this opp touch), NOT an authority check (whose action is this). A partner org is legitimately in tenancy and must still accept its own invitation — that rule cannot live here and is enforced by assertAcceptingForSelf in lib/connect-orgs.ts (ace#2954).

rules.name: labs-synthetic-allowlist
rules._operator_values_doc: The ONLY domains admitted on a labs allowlist (ace-web dropped the per-opp labs_allowed_domains on 2026-10-08, so Labs stays Dimagi-only): Dimagi staff (@dimagi.com and @dimagi-associate.com, owner 2026-10-16 — associates are Dimagi, as lib/destructive-guards.ts DIMAGI_OWNER_DOMAINS already says) and ACE's own mailbox domain ({agent_email_domain} = config/agent.json email). Neither widens a partner's view, and ACE must stay on every list or it locks itself out of its own synthetic opps — synthetic_set_allowed_domains REPLACES the list (ace#2713).

rules.name: connect-create-organization
rules.refuse_when_bound: connect_create_organization makes a NEW Connect org, which is outside every opp's tenancy by definition. It is for ACE-owned orgs only (e.g. ACE's synthetic winner org, ACE_CONNECT_LLO_ORG), created once in an unbound session, never inside an opp-bound one.

rules.name: labs-create-solicitation
rules._args_doc: A call is owned by the opp's PM org (ace-web tenancy connect_pm_org). program_id must be one of the opp's Connect programs (tenancy connect_program_ids, ace-web#914); an opp whose tenancy has no programs refuses as not set up (logged only in warn mode) — bin/ace-bind --add-program fills it when ACE creates the program. award_response / update_solicitation / create_response name the winner by its Connect org INTEGER id (connect-labs #2605), which no tenancy field holds, so they are not slug-checked here; the call itself is owned by the PM org that created_solicitation was checked against.

rules.name: labs-create-response
rules._args_doc: create_response's program_id is 'accepted for compatibility; not needed' upstream, so it is usually absent (absent = unchecked). When given, it must be one of the opp's programs (tenancy connect_program_ids).

rules.name: labs-supply-chain-org-upsert
rules._args_doc: A labs org row bound to a Connect org must bind to one of the opp's orgs, or to ACE's own synthetic winner org (ACE_CONNECT_LLO_ORG from the installed .env — an ACE-owned org, never a partner's, so admitting it widens no partner's view; unset admits nothing). Listed BEFORE labs-supply-chain-writes so this rule, not the generic one, matches.

rules.name: labs-supply-chain-writes
rules._args_doc: Every supply-chain write is scoped by program_id, and labs keeps no delete for tenders, quotes, awards, contracts, shipments, receipts, invoices or payments (spec 2026-10-18 § F6), so a write into the wrong program cannot be cleaned up — this is the rule that guards it, against tenancy connect_program_ids (dimagi-internal/ace-web#914). Absent or empty refuses as not set up, like any other tenancy field (warn mode only logs); connect-program-setup adds the opp's program with bin/ace-bind --add-program, and ace-web's backfill_connect_program_ids fills existing opps from opp.yaml. The write/read split is pinned against the full live tool list in test/hooks/tenancy-guard.test.ts. programme_runner_set's org_id is a labs org pk, which no tenancy field holds; only its program_id is checked.
